All parameter-like objects exposed to users and scripting are RefCounted. For once because users cant be expected to manage and free those manually and also because the script binding system can not bind to more native C++ things.

That code here in particular is just a workaround because there is no real 2D NavigationServer so we need to create 3D objects behind the scene to query the NavigationServer3D.

Same as with the Parameters, things like this that are exposed to script users and the binding system need to be RefCounted. To avoid new object creation on the exposed API all the time we just update the objects in the query instead of returning new things. There are older discussions e.g. physics ray API, that returns stuff with functions which is really bad for performance at the exposed API, especially with languages like C# that struggle with their garbage collector. Internally we can do what we want but everything that is part of a bind_method() is trouble.

Because it did not work. The compiler vomited all over the place trying to give the CoW Vector to the LocalVector parameter. Theoretically the LocalVector template should convert but it didn't. The internal simplify functions all use LocalVector to avoid the CoW farm. It is only the server api that need to stick to CoW Vector as scripts can not work with LocalVector.
Yes, script exposed API can only work with CoW Vector, aka PackedArrays. They can not use LocalVector.

Most of the copies here are intentional as this is the place to step from user land to server internals.

The RefCounted Parameters and Result are user exposed. They can be broken at any time by users that do funky stuff with them.

This is why we immediatly copy from the parameters and later copy back to the result object not using anything from them in the actual server internals.

This will be even more important with threading where we can trust users even less to not break things. The system can be seen in the navmesh baking that uses similar logic but already uses the task for threaded bakes.
Agree
The path points at this end stage of the pathbuilder are all arranged from target to start so we need to invert them all because users need the path from start to target.

The LocalVector here is from a `PathQuerySlot` of the map that has already memory for all the temp query data. If it was used by any other query already it will have e.g. index or other properties set from the previous path search. We need to `reset()` all those values back to the defaut before we can use it.
Lets do this "distance to distance_squared" in another PR as it is all over the place in those path function.
